name: Johns Hopkins University & University of Pennsylvania Schools of Nursing Information Session
description:
Co-sponsored by Health Professions Advising and the Career Development Office

Join admissions representatives from the Johns Hopkins University School of Nursing and the University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing for an in-person information session exploring pathways into the nursing profession through accelerated entry programs.

Representatives will provide an overview of their nationally recognized nursing programs, including accelerated Master of Nursing and other graduate entry pathways for students who have completed a bachelor's degree in another discipline. The session will also discuss admissions requirements, prerequisite coursework, clinical training, financial aid, career opportunities, and what distinguishes each institution's approach to nursing education.

Students considering careers in nursing, advanced practice nursing, public health, or healthcare leadership are encouraged to attend. This is an excellent opportunity to learn about the profession, ask questions directly of admissions officers, and gain insights into preparing a competitive application.

Guest Speaker: Chris Jermyn, Associate Director of Admissions, University of Pennsylvania School of Nursing
Laura Panozzo, Associate Director Admissions, Johns Hopkins University School of Nursing

name: Humanism & Health Speaker Series
description:
The inaugural session of the Humanism & Health Speaker Series will take place virtually on October 16, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. PT and will feature Victoria A. Smith, MD, Associate Medical Director for Primary Care at Ochsner Health, in conversation with Soka University of America Student Fellow Kiarra Hoes.

Co-hosted by Soka University of America and the WHO Collaborating Centre for Healthy Cities and Urban Policy Research at the Institute of Science Tokyo, the Humanism & Health Speaker Series examines how health professionals and leaders translate humanistic values into practice across clinical care, health systems, public and global health, and planetary health. Through an interview-based conversation, Dr. Smith will discuss how humanism informs her approach to patient care and health care leadership.

description:
Ohana Stories on OC Talk Radio presents a community screening of a powerful feature-length documentary, Sanctuary. Producer Autumn McAlpin welcomes the community to this event, with cast members who will join a post-screening Q&A. 

Sanctuary is a feature-length documentary that exposes the plight of LGBTQIA+ individuals within modern faith systems—told through the eyes of a visionary architect whose passion project becomes a lifeline. As doctrine collides with identity, a sacred space rises from rejection, offering refuge and hope. Register today!

name: Annotations of Hope: Dr. Nahum Chandler on Du Bois's "Of the Coming of John"
description:
A lecture by Dr. Nahum Chandler

W. E. B. Du Bois’s short story “Of the Coming of John “is about a young man’s journey, from a happy go lucky small-town boy with never a care in the world, through an initial failure in his first year of college, to his return to school and discovery of himself anew in the world of thought. It is the discovery of what Du Bois elsewhere describes as a kind of “double-consciousness.” This short story is the masterpiece of Du Bois’s book The Souls of Black Folk: Essays and Sketches of 1903, a classic text in American thought — a book and short story about hope for the future of America at the turn to the 20th century.
 
The story is about 20 pages long. An audio version is available. The text can be found online in a reliable scholarly edition, including through Ikeda Library. Please read or listen before the lecture. Music as reference and hearing will be integral to the lecture.

name: Asian Americas: Discussing Papers from Graduate Students at CalState Los Angeles
description: Co-sponsored by the Pacific Basin Area and the Pacific Basin Research Center, this conference will bring two CalState Los Angeles graduate students focusing on Asian migrant communities to share their research with undergraduates, particularly students in the Intro to the Pacific Basin course. SUA students will serve as discussants before concluding the evening with a cafeteria dinner to discuss graduate studies in Los Angeles. The presentations feature Ari Muramoto examining how Guadalajara’s Chinese community contradicted Mexico's antichinismo movement through local integration and resistance to the California borderlands model, and Henry Truong utilizing oral histories to document a Vietnamese refugee family's resettlement and business establishment in a rural California desert and military town.
